symptom

The symptoms you mentioned could be related to several conditions. Please tell me more about the specific symptoms: Are they pain? Difficulty urinating or passing stools/gas? Bleeding from the anus, especially after a bowel movement? Or something else entirely? Once I understand what is causing your problem, we can discuss appropriate management and potential medications based on our standard guidelines for Nigerian primary healthcare.
what is the treatment for malaria

Di system identify this as: Malaria
Confidence: 100%
Severity: Manageable at this level

TREATMENT:

DRUGS:
  + Prompt parasitological confirmation by microscopy or RDTs before treatment
  + Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACTs)
  + Artemether-Lumefantrine (AL) is the medicine of choice
  + Artesunate-Amodiaquine (AA), Dihydroartemisinin Piperaquine and Artesunate-Pyronaridine are alternatives
  + Pre-make dem refer am go hospital treatment (Rectal Artesunate, Artesunate IM, Artemether IM or Quinine IM)

SUPPORTIVE CARE:
  + Paracetamol (oral/rectal) for symptomatic relief
  + If temperature is >38.5°C, wipe with wet towel, and fan to lower the temperature
  + Nurse in cardiac position for Pulmonary oedema

WATCH OUT FOR:
  ⚠  Mefloquine make you make you no use am if di patient had cerebral malaria because of the increased risk of seizure, encephalopathy and psychosis.

TESTS Wey Fit Needed:
  - Blood smear for malaria parasites
  - Packed cell volume; haemoglobin concentration
  - White cell count with differentials

HOW TO PREVENT AM:
  + Reduce the frequency of mosquito bites by make you no useing exposure to mosquitoes at their peak feeding times.
  + Use insect repellants.
  + Put on suitable clothing.

Di system identify this as: Acute Abdomen
Confidence: 50%
Severity: Consider make dem refer am go hospital to hospital

TREATMENT:

WETIN YOU FIT DO WITHOUT DRUG:
  + Resuscitation and general measures
  + Rehydration and correction of electrolyte derangements
  + Correct shock by giving crystalloids or colloid
  + Maintenance fluids based on degree of dehydration
  + Correct electrolyte deficits (especially potassium)

DRUGS:
  + Commence broad spectrum, intravenous antibiotics (no go give am aminoglycosides until urine output is adequate)

SUPPORTIVE CARE:
  + dey check closely by repeated examinations and electronic dey check to identify adequate resuscitation
  + make you no use time wasting and identify non-responding patients
  + dey check parameters for adequate rehydration: cardio-respiratory stability, pulse rate, blood pressure, central venous pressure, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure, urine output, hydration status, skin turgor, sensorium

TESTS Wey Fit Needed:
  - Plain radiography of abdomen: Supine and upright films to identify features of intestinal obstruction (dilated bowel loops and multiple fluid levels); a radio-opaque shadow may be seen in the region of the urinary tract in ureteric colic
  - Plain radiography of chest: An upright film may identify gas under the diaphragm in gastrointestinal perforation and look for chest infection
  - Abdomino-pelvic ultrasonography: Should help ascertain the cause of pain (e.g. cholecystitis, gynaecologic conditions, urinary calculi, degenerating masses); may identify injured solid organ in trauma
